precepts.text: For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. Our people may see what we do as foolishness. But God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. That is our purpose. To be sent to preach God's word, to save the believers, to save the elect. And you have to take pride in it.
precepts.point: And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth. Our job is to raise up the tribes and restore the preserved of Israel. A light to the Gentiles: that is the scattered Israelites. That thou mayest be my salvation: that you may be a saviour.

note.label: Give Diligence

precepts.why:
Romans 10 asks, how shall they hear except they be sent? We have been sent to the four corners of the earth, sent from the beginning to be saviours, to “raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” And Paul shows the way God chose to do it: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

Our people may see what we do as foolishness. Someone may say, I’ve just been called to do this to fold. No. God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.

That is our purpose. Preach God’s word. To be sent to preach God’s word, to save the believers, to save the elect. That is our goal and our mission, and you have to take pride in it.

So when Isaiah says the servant shall be “my salvation unto the end of the earth”, this is how: not by the wisdom of the world, which never knew God, but by the preaching of the prophets whom God formed from the womb and sent. Standing on the corner looking like a fool preaching his word is exactly what pleases him, and it is how Jacob is brought again to him.

precepts.text: But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God. Christ is the wisdom of God. So if any man be in Christ he is a new creature, because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.
precepts.point: But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked. Reprove with equity means you are not partial. So having the spirit of the Lord, you are not going to be in partiality. You are going to have knowledge and understanding. You are going to obtain, you are going to retain, and you are going to apply. And it shows you the power he will have as well.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.why:
“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

precepts.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” Precepts were called for from the brothers, and the first was Paul's own plea to the same Corinthians: “Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you”.

That fits the body. The members are many, but they speak the same thing, and there are no divisions among them. Diversity does not mean division: a different administration, dealing with something you don't deal with, is not separate from you. And different roles do not mean inequality; no function or operation in the body is unneeded.

That is why, wherever you travel among us, it should carry the same teachings: we are one body, in one mind, speaking the same thing. It all goes back to endeavouring to keep the unity, until we all come “unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”.

precepts.text: Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Who is this wisdom we are to seek? Christ is also known as wisdom: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

So when Sirach speaks of wisdom exalting her children, and when Proverbs has wisdom saying “By me princes rule”, it is Christ speaking. The Lord is the one who sets up all the kings and all the princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God by whom they rule.

To seek wisdom is to seek Christ. Those who seek him are the ones wisdom lays hold of, and the children she exalts are the ones he calls: the called, both Jews and Greeks.

precepts.text: When the seventh month was come, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Ezra 3:1 says the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem. Imagine how much could be done with one mind, one spirit and one judgment.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Paul beseeches the brethren “that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.” When did we all speak the same thing? In the time of King David and King Solomon, when we ruled the nations. At one time we were unified, and we put the heathen, the other nations, in subjection. Are we unified today?

Ezra shows what that looks like: “And when the seventh month was come, and the children of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.” As one man. Think about it on the Sabbath day: we come to hear the word of the Lord, and they gathered themselves together as one man.

Imagine us being perfectly joined together as one man. Imagine how much we could get done if we thought as one man, with the same mind, the same spirit and the same judgment. That is called unity.

It is the same unity Paul calls for in Ephesians 4: “Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace”, “Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man”. That perfect man is the one man. Brothers are going to offend brothers and sisters are going to offend sisters; get over it. There are bigger things to worry about than your feelings. Keep the unity no matter what, for the perfecting of the saints.

precepts.text: It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.
precepts.point: This is not a time of peace but of war; not physical war, but uniting, keeping the law and waiting on the Redeemer.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
How do we bring about that change? How do you fight a nuke? How do you fight powers that can turn off your lights, run your economy and take your resources right under your nose while you say thank you? With something small and simple: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

It was God’s wisdom that the world would not know him, that they would purposely not be able to understand. It is given unto us to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; he made everything a mystery so that only his elect can unseal what the Bible says. And just as it pleases him to see a man lifted up in power so that he can take him down, it pleases him to save by the foolishness of preaching. That is how we get our identity back. That is how we come back.

So look at the brothers in the streets. Don’t think those efforts are small; they are making an impact. Even if your camp doesn’t have a lot of foot traffic, none of it is in vain, none of it is void. You go out, you preach, you gather, you fish. Even if there are scarce fish in that water, if you know there is a spot where fish be, you stay there until you catch at least one. You are not trying to come home empty.

It starts with preaching and then it escalates. First we repent, then we get the honor. We do not fight physically now: we repent now, we fight through preaching, and God fights for us later. Then comes the honor of Psalm 149, “a twoedged sword in their hand; To execute vengeance upon the heathen”, for “this honour have all his saints.” When he shall roar, “the children shall tremble from the west”, the western hemisphere, “and I will place them in their houses, saith the Lord”: our tribes, our royal heritage and our identity given back to us, the sons of the living God.

precepts.text: That all speak the same thing and that there be no divisions among you. The decree only worked because every man there had the same mind.
precepts.point: Our forefathers had to make that decision and every man there had to have the same mind. That is the decision in front of us too: get to camp, get out to war, endure hardness, and drop the victim mindset.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

precepts.text: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles: Christ called himself the wisdom of God.
precepts.point: Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God, so the wisdom created in Proverbs 8 and in Sirach 24 is Christ.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: Speak the same thing, no divisions, perfectly joined together in the same mind and the same judgment; that is the camp moving in one direction.
precepts.point: All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
A camp moves in one unison, in one direction. “Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.”

Speak the same thing, no divisions, perfectly joined together in the same mind and the same judgment: that is the body moving as a camp. The Most High is very particular about the most holy things, and the order of the camp is how the body moves in one direction.

precepts.text: That ye all speak the same thing: John the Revelator and Moses were speaking the same thing, and Christ spoke out of the Old Testament.
precepts.point: The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove Matthew 18:11 and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.”

That is what the prophets did. John the Revelator and Moses were speaking the same thing, neither add nor diminish, and Christ spoke out of the Old Testament. Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ and John, across millenniums and captivities, all speak the same thing, perfectly joined together in the same mind and the same judgment. That consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes.

So we speak the same thing too: not adding to the word and not diminishing from it, that there be no divisions among us.

precepts.text: Not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble are called; God hath chosen the foolish, the weak, the base, and the despised things of the world to confound the mighty.
precepts.point: The Lord commissions him: go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites; have not I sent thee? Gideon answers with his pedigree: my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house. That is a defeated mentality, and we all have to overcome it, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon answers the Lord with his pedigree: “my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.” That is a defeated mentality, and it is the very thing Paul answers. “For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called.”

“But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are.”

The poor family in Manasseh and the least in his father's house is exactly whom God chooses. We all have to overcome that defeated mentality, because every one of us was called for a reason, to put a brick in for the kingdom.

precepts.text: Not many mighty are called; the Most High did not choose the giants that were in the earth, he chose Israel, few in number; that is how he operates.
precepts.point: David was also young when the spirit came on him, and that is nothing new either; the Most High does not choose the ones everybody expects, for the spirit of Christ was in the prophets he selected.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty”.

Not many mighty are called. The Most High did not choose the giants that were in the earth; he chose Israel, few in number. He passed over Jesse’s older, bigger sons and chose the youngest, who kept the sheep. That is how he operates.

precepts.text: Israel is to be of one accord, perfectly joined together in the same mind and judgment.
precepts.point: They were with David three days eating and drinking, and their brethren brought bread, figs, raisins, wine, oil, and cattle abundantly, for there was joy in Israel. The joy came from being of one mind, which is why the feast days are to be kept with gladness.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

precepts.why:
“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.” Israel is to be of one accord.

That is what the tribes were at Hebron. The men of war “came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.” Even the tribes beyond Jordan were of one accord with the rest. That is why we must be of one accord, for Christ is going to sit on the throne of David his father.

They were with David three days, eating and drinking, and their brethren brought bread, figs, raisins, wine, oil and cattle abundantly, “for there was joy in Israel.” The joy came from being of one mind, which is why the feast days are to be kept with gladness.

precepts.text: Speak the same thing, be of one mind and one judgment with no divisions, the same unity that gave Israel one heart to serve the Most High.
precepts.point: The great congregation removes the altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and casts them into the brook Kidron.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

precepts.why:
“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.” Speak the same thing, be of one mind and one judgment, with no divisions.

That is the same unity that gave Israel one heart to serve the Most High. “Also in Judah the hand of God was to give them one heart to do the commandment of the king and of the princes, by the word of the Lord.” And “there assembled at Jerusalem much people to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great congregation.”

Not everyone received it. The posts “passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun: but they laughed them to scorn, and mocked them”, the same mockery Israel meets today when the truth is preached. “Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem.” And being of one mind, the congregation “took away the altars that were in Jerusalem, and all the altars for incense took they away, and cast them into the brook Kidron.”

precepts.text: Not many wise, mighty, or noble are called, for the Most High has chosen the foolish and weak things of the world to confound the wise and mighty, so those on this reading are of no less value than anyone.
precepts.point: When our people do well financially, get a good education, and buy into the pick-yourself-up-by-the-bootstraps idea that everyone has the same opportunity, the smart ones are removed from the ghetto so they will not be there to cause the uprising.

note.label: Ezekiel 17: The Riddle of the Two Eagles

precepts.why:
The enemy takes the mighty, the best and the brightest. But look at who the Most High calls: “not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called”. Instead, “God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty”.

So the oppressor removing the smart ones from the ghetto does not stop the Most High. He works with those the world counts foolish and weak, and confounds the mighty with them.

Those on this reading are of no less value than anyone. The mighty of the land were carried away and taught the tongue of the Chaldeans; those the world counts foolish and weak are the ones He has chosen.

precepts.text: Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.
precepts.point: The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power, which is why the same sentence can say both.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
How can the same sentence say the Word was with God and the Word was God? “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.” Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.

The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power. That is why John can say both at once. The Word was with God in the beginning, and the Word was God's own wisdom and power.

precepts.text: For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
The Jews answered him, “What sign shewest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?” Asking after signs was their habit, and the epistle names it: “For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom”.

That is why they came at him with that question after he cleansed the temple. The Jews require a sign. Paul knew his people, and that is the very thing we see them doing here.

precepts.text: Paul, Christ, Peter, and James all speak the same thing, that there be no divisions, being perfectly joined together, because they spoke as Christ spoke.
precepts.point: Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.”

Paul, Christ, Peter and James all speak the same thing, because they spoke as Christ spoke. The disciples all said what Christ said, perfectly joined together in the same mind, and that is how the rulers knew they had been with Jesus.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why: “for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” You have seen the brothers Christ uses, but you have not seen Christ. Rejecting all those brothers while claiming you only love Christ does not fulfill this command. It is the same problem as claiming Christ as a faction against the men he sent.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why: Philip heard the eunuch reading Esaias and asked whether he understood. “How can I, except some man should guide me?” The eunuch asked Philip to sit with him. He needed a man to guide him in the scriptures. Having a Bible in your hand does not remove the need for teachers appointed by God. That is why the party claiming only Christ was wrong along with the other factions.
